Disney+ is $12.49 with ads, Premium $21.49 or $214.99 a year, the Hulu bundle $12.99 or $21.99, ESPN bundles to $44.99, NFL+ bundles $45.99 up. Every price on one page.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Disney+ has two plans of its own and nine more that wrap it with Hulu, ESPN, HBO Max or NFL+. As of October 10, 2026, Disney+‘s plans and prices page lists Disney+ (With Ads) at $12.49 a month, Disney+ Premium at $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year, the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99 or $21.99, the ESPN bundles from $21.99 to $44.99, the HBO Max bundles at $21.99 or $34.99, and two NFL+ Premium bundles at $45.99 and $54.99. These are the prices for new subscriptions since September 23, 2026; the page says anyone who signed up earlier sees the change “in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.” This guide puts every price on one page, works out the arithmetic Disney’s page does not, and notes where the page is silent. If you are leaving, the billing paths are in our Disney+ cancellation guide.

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49 a month, no annual option listed

By WDWMAGIC Staff· Wednesday September 23, 2026 12:44pm ET·"Disney+"

 Disney+ prices have risen across most plans as of September 23, 2026. Premium tiers jumped 13.2%, while existing subscribers keep their current rate until October 21, 2026. 

Photos / 3 in this gallery

 

Disney has raised prices on several Disney+ and bundle subscription plans. 

The Disney+ price increase applies to new subscriptions starting today, September 23, 2026. If you already have a Disney+ subscription, the new pricing will show up in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.

### New Disney+ Pricing and Percentage Increases

Here's what changed, including how much each plan went up by percentage:

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49, up from $11.99 — a 4.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Monthly (No Ads): $21.49, up from $18.99 — a 13.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Annual (No Ads): $214.99, up from $189.99 — a 13.2% increase

The Premium plans, both monthly and annual, saw the largest percentage jump at over 13%. The ad-supported Disney+ plan had the smallest increase, at just over 4%.

### When You'll See the Change

New subscribers pay the updated prices right away. If you're a current subscriber, your rate stays the same until your next billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026. Check your account settings for your exact renewal date so you know when the new price takes effect.

# Disney+ Price Increase Hits October 21: Why the $21.99 Hulu Bundle Beats $21.49 Premium, and How to Switch or Cancel First (2026)

 By Jordan Lee October 12, 2026 October 12, 2026 

Short answer: Existing Disney+ subscribers pay the new prices from their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Premium goes from $18.99 to $21.49 a month. The plan with ads goes from $11.99 to $12.49. Here’s the odd part: the Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle is $21.99, just 50 cents more than Disney+ Premium alone. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads didn’t change at $12.99. If you pay for Premium by itself, the bundle or the ad tier is almost always the better deal now.

A $2.50 bump doesn’t sound like much. Over a year it’s $30, and Disney has now raised Disney+ prices roughly once a year since launch.

But the more interesting change isn’t the hike itself. Disney priced its plans so that Disney+ Premium on its own now looks like a bad deal next to the bundle. Once you see the numbers side by side, the “what should I do before October 21” question mostly answers itself.

Below is every new price, the plan math for the three most common situations, and how to switch or cancel cleanly before your renewal date.

## In This Comparison

- When does the Disney+ price increase hit existing subscribers?
- How much does each Disney+ plan cost now?
- Is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle cheaper than Disney+ Premium alone?
- Should you switch to the annual plan?
- How do I switch plans or cancel before my renewal?
- Picking the Cheapest Plan for How You Actually Watch
- Tips
- Warnings
- FAQ
- Sources

## When does the Disney+ price increase hit existing subscribers?

Existing U.S. Disney+ subscribers are charged the new prices starting with their first billing date on or after October 21, 2026, while new subscribers have paid the higher rates since September 23, 2026, according to Disney’s announcement as reported by CBS News on September 23, 2026.

So the exact day depends on your billing date. If you’re billed on the 5th, your first higher charge lands November 5. If you’re billed on the 22nd, it lands October 22.

That’s useful. Most people have a week or more to decide.

## How much does each Disney+ plan cost now?

As of October 2026, Disney+ Premium costs $21.49 a month and Disney+ with ads costs $12.49 a month in the U.S., up from $18.99 and $11.99, while the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stays at $12.99 a month, per Disney’s figures reported by CBS News and Variety.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$6.00 |
| Disney+ Premium (no ads) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$30.00 |
| Disney+ and Hulu bundle (with ads) | $12.99 | $12.99 | $0 |

Prices from Disney’s September 23, 2026 announcement as reported by CBS News and Variety. Yearly change is our calculation (monthly difference × 12), before tax.

## Is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle cheaper than Disney+ Premium alone?

The Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle costs $21.99 a month after the October 2026 increase, only $0.50 more than Disney+ Premium alone at $21.49, so anyone paying for ad-free Disney+ by itself can add ad-free Hulu for 50 cents.

When I compared the old and new tables, I found that the gap used to be bigger in the other direction. Under the old prices, the Premium bundle cost $1.00 more than Disney+ Premium alone ($19.99 vs $18.99). Now it’s half that.

Disney+ and Hulu Prices Rose in the U.S. — What Each Plan Costs Now | RED REACTIONS

# Disney+ and Hulu Prices Rose in the U.S. — What Each Plan Costs Now

Disney+ and Hulu's U.S. ad-free plans now cost $21.49 a month. Compare September 2026 standalone and bundle prices, unchanged tiers, promotions and billing timing.

SA By Sara Avegaard Published September 24, 2026 at 7:08 PM CEST 3 min read

Official Hulu on Disney+ logo showing both streaming brands together. Disney+ Press

Disney+ and Hulu’s U.S. standalone plans now cost $12.49 a month with ads or $21.49 a month for Premium. The ad-free price is $2.50 higher than before; the ad-supported price is up 50 cents. The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads remains $12.99 a month, while its Premium bundle rose to $21.99. New subscriber prices took effect September 23, 2026. Existing subscribers see the change on their next monthly bill, according to TheWrap’s price-change report.

These are standard U.S. monthly prices, before tax or any eligibility-limited offer. Disney currently advertises lower six-month introductory prices for some bundles; those offers renew at the regular rates shown below.

## What Changed in September 2026?

| U.S. plan | Previous monthly price | Current monthly price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Disney+ Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Hulu Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Disney+ + Hulu with ads | $12.99 | $12.99 | No change |
| Disney+ + Hulu Premium | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select with ads | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select Premium | $29.99 | $32.99 | +$3.00 |

The current rates come from Disney’s plan listings and Hulu. Previous rates and the timing of the increase come from contemporaneous reporting. Disney+ Premium also has a current $214.99 annual option; the table compares monthly plans only.

## Which Bundles Stayed the Same?

Disney’s current site still lists Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Unlimited at $35.99 a month with ads on Disney+ and Hulu, and $44.99 for the Premium Disney+/Hulu combination. Both Unlimited bundle prices were unchanged in the September price-change reporting. ESPN Select and Unlimited are different plans; do not compare their prices as if they contain the same sports access.

The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads also stayed at $12.99. That is just 50 cents more than either ad-supported service alone at $12.49. The Premium duo at $21.99 is likewise 50 cents more than either $21.49 standalone Premium plan. That is a price comparison, not a claim that every viewer needs both services.

## What About HBO Max and Live TV?

Disney currently lists its Disney+ + Hulu + HBO Max bundle at $21.99 a month with ads or $34.99 without ads. Its Hulu + Live TV package, which includes Disney+ and ESPN Select, is $99.99 a month; the Premium Live TV combination is $109.99. Check the exact included services and any trial or promotion at checkout, because these are different packages from the two-service bundles above.

## When Will Existing Subscribers Pay More?

The September 23 rates applied to new U.S. sign-ups immediately. Existing monthly subscribers do not all get charged on the announcement date: the higher amount appears on their next billing cycle. Check your own account notice and renewal date for the precise charge. These prices do not describe Disney+ or Hulu subscriptions outside the U.S.

Disney’s current bundle page also offers eligible customers six months of the Disney+/Hulu ad-supported duo at $11.99 a month or the Premium duo at $19.99 a month, billed for the full six-month term. After that, they renew at $12.99 and $21.99 a month respectively. Those temporary prices are not the new standard rates.

Disney Plus Subscription Cost - Budget Seniors

# Disney Plus Subscription Cost

 Budget Seniors, September 26, 2026 September 26, 2026 

Disney Plus launched in 2019 at $6.99 a month. It has since raised prices six times, and a seventh increase was announced for late 2026. Before you subscribe — or keep subscribing — it helps to know exactly what each plan covers, where the bundles actually save money, and which discount paths most people never check. The answers are less straightforward than the sign-up page implies.

 The short answer Disney Plus currently offers two standalone plans in the U.S.: Basic (with ads) at $12/month and Premium (no ads) at $19/month or $189.99/year. Bundles with Hulu start at $13/month — just $1 more than Basic alone — and add the entire Hulu library. A new price increase announced in late September 2026 will raise Basic to $12.49 and Premium to $21.49 for new subscribers imminently; verify current prices at disneyplus.com before subscribing. 

 Editorial Review Sandra Merritt — Streaming & Consumer Subscription Analyst 13 Years Covering U.S. Streaming Services · Subscription Pricing Research · Independent Consumer Affairs Contributor 

$12/mo Basic plan with ads — full library, 1080p, 2 streams

$19/mo Premium — no ads on-demand, 4K, 4 streams, downloads

$189.99 Annual Premium — saves ~$38 vs 12 monthly payments

$13/mo Duo Basic bundle — Disney+ and Hulu, both with ads

## Key Answers People Search For First

Six price increases since launch, a new bundle structure, a password-sharing crackdown, and a seventh increase already announced — there is more complexity in Disney Plus pricing than most people realize. These answers get to what actually matters.

1 How much does Disney Plus cost per month right now?

Two standalone plans exist in the U.S. Basic at $12 per month includes ads — roughly 4 minutes of commercials per hour — and streams at up to 1080p Full HD on two devices simultaneously. Premium at $19 per month (or $189.99 per year) removes ads from all on-demand content, unlocks 4K UHD with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos audio, allows four simultaneous streams, and adds offline downloads on iOS and Android. Both plans cover the full Disney+ library and support up to seven user profiles. Note: Disney announced another price increase in late September 2026, set to raise Basic to $12.49 and Premium to $21.49 — check disneyplus.com for the current rate before signing up.

2 Is there a free trial for Disney Plus?

No standard free trial exists for direct sign-ups. Disney removed the 7-day free trial in 2021 and has not reinstated it. If you sign up at disneyplus.com today, you pay from day one. However, partner promotions do offer limited free access. Verizon customers on eligible unlimited plans (Ultimate, Plus, or Welcome) can add the Disney Bundle as a $10/month perk — check My Verizon’s perks tab before paying full price. DirecTV subscribers can access a 5-day free trial window through DirecTV’s MyEntertainment package. Promotional bundle pricing — discounted first months — also appears periodically for new subscribers. Always search your carrier name plus “Disney Plus deal” before signing up at full price.

3 Is paying annually actually worth it — and what happens if I cancel early?

The annual plan only applies to Disney+ Premium. At $189.99 per year, you save about $38 compared to paying $19 monthly for twelve months. That’s roughly two free months. The trade-off is real: Disney does not issue prorated refunds for unused months if you cancel an annual plan early. Cancel after six months and you’ve paid for the full year. The annual option makes sense if you’ve already been on Disney+ for a year and watch consistently. It is less sensible if you’re trying the service for the first time, or if you tend to subscribe-binge-cancel-repeat. The Basic plan has no annual option — it’s month-to-month only.

Price of Disney Plus, Hulu: Services Raising Prices in October 2025

 Sep 23, 2025 10:35am PT 

# Disney+, Hulu Are Hiking Prices Again Next Month 

 By Todd Spangler 

 

 Courtesy of Disney 

 It’s that time of year again, apparently: Disney is raising the prices of its Disney+ and Hulu plans in the U.S., including most bundles, as of next month.

 The standalone Disney+ with ads service is rising from $9.99 to $11.99/month on Oct. 21, 2025, while the Disney+ Premium (without ads) is going from $15.99 to $18.99/month. The Hulu standalone plan with ads is increasing from $9.99 to $11.99/month as of the same date; the premium version of Hulu with no ads will remain at $18.99 per month. 

 In addition, the price of ESPN Select (the service formerly known as ESPN+, which has a more limited content lineup than the recently launched ESPN Unlimited all-in app) will increase from $11.99 to $12.99 per month on Oct. 21. For now, the introductory price of the Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited bundle with ads will remain $29.99 per month (for the first 12 months). 

### Popular on Variety 

 Reached by Variety, a rep for Disney declined to provide additional comment on the price hikes. It’s the third time in three years Disney is raising the prices of the streaming services in the U.S., after price hikes for Disney+ and Hulu in October 2024 and in October 2023. Disney provided notifications of the latest price hikes Tuesday on its customer support sites.

 The company has been planning the fee hikes for weeks. But the price increases were announced after many Disney+ and Hulu users in recent days said they were cancelling their service in the wake of Disney and ABC’s suspension of Jimmy Kimmel over comments the late-night host made about the killer of Charlie Kirk. That came after the head of FCC dangled the threat of investigations into ABC stations if they didn’t drop Kimmel; following his remarks, local TV station groups Nexstar Media and Sinclair said they would preempt the program. Disney said Kimmel’s show will be returning to ABC Tuesday evening but Nexstar and Sinclair said they will not air “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” for the time being in protest. 

 Disney, after completing the full acquisition of Hulu in a deal with Comcast this June, is now in the midst of fusing the two services together: In 2026, Disney expects to shut down Hulu as a standalone app and service and fully merge Hulu into Disney+. (According to Disney, you will still be able to purchase Disney+ and Hulu as standalone plans.)
